claims.text: Monte Carlo simulations can introduce and evolve chemical short-range ordering in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed Monte Carlo treatment promotes HfTi and TiZr clustering.
HfTi and TiZr clustering produces percolation pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
The clustering modifies local atomic arrangements.
The resulting percolation pathways are conductive.
Conductive pathways alter the electronic or thermal conductivity behavior of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Clustering mitigates anomalous conductivity effects introduced by oxygen impurities and intrinsic defects.
Monte Carlo-induced CSRO will improve agreement between predicted and measured conductivity relative to perfect-crystal analytical approaches.
The proposed accuracy improvement will apply across the nearly 0–200 K regime.
The proposed accuracy improvement will apply across the 300–1200 K regime.
The proposed model will capture defect-driven conductivity anomalies in HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Existing analytical predictions are based solely on perfect, defect-free crystal models.
Perfect-crystal models have been unable to accurately capture conductivity nuances in real, disordered HfNbTaTiZr samples.
Experimental conductivity measurements are available for specimens with and without 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed approach is applicable only to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing no more than 1 wt.% oxygen within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Outside the stated temperature ranges or above 1 wt.% oxygen, additional mechanisms may dominate and the hypothesis may fail.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant accuracy improvement over the perfect-crystal baseline in both temperature regimes and both sample types would falsify the hypothesis.
